---
title: "Fire findings (pilot)"
subtitle: "Buildings vacated after fires had far more hazardous HPD violations than their neighbors"
---

```{python}
from _pilot import *
from fire_data import blocks as fire_blocks
from collapse_data import blocks as collapse_blocks
fire_rows = score(fire_blocks, FIRE_FEATURES)
fire = {r["feature"]: r for r in fire_rows}
c = fire["HPD Class C violations per apartment"]
top = sum(p == 1.0 for p in c["per_case"])
```

Of the `{python} len(fire_blocks)` buildings in the pilot, `{python} top` had the **highest** rate
of Class C ("immediately hazardous") HPD violations per apartment among comparable buildings on
their block. DOB records alone did not set them apart.

## How each record ranked

Each fire building was compared with similar residential buildings on its own block
(`{python} n_controls(fire_blocks)` in total), using only records dated before 2025. A rank of 50%
means typical for the block; 100% means higher than every neighbor.

```{python}
#| fig-alt: "Dot chart: HPD Class C violations per apartment rank highest, near 87 percent; DOB records rank near 50 to 60 percent."
fig = rank_chart(fire_rows, "HPD violations set fire buildings apart; DOB records did not")
```

Blue dots are unlikely to be chance (permutation test, p < 0.05); gray dots are not.

## Building by building

```{python}
import pandas as pd
names = {"BK": "Brooklyn", "BX": "Bronx", "MN": "Manhattan", "QN": "Queens"}
rows = []
for (b, d), cc, sm in zip(fire_blocks.items(), c["per_case"], [None]*len(fire_blocks)):
    boro, blk = b.split(" ")[0].split("-")
    u, abc, cnt = d["lots"][d["case"]][:3]
    rows.append({"Location": f"{names[boro]}, block {blk}", "Apartments": u,
                 "Class C violations": cnt, "Class C per apt.": round(cnt / u, 1),
                 "Rank on block": f"{cc:.0%}", "Neighbors compared": len(d["lots"]) - 1})
pd.DataFrame(rows).style.hide(axis="index").format({"Class C per apt.": "{:.1f}"})
```

The one clear exception is the Queens building, which had a nearly clean HPD record before its fire.

## What it means, and what it doesn't

- **The signal is HPD-specific.** For fires, conditions tenants report to HPD (wiring, detectors,
  doors, heat, general disrepair) carry the signal. In a matching pilot on structural collapses,
  the pattern reversed: DOB history mattered and HPD alone did not.
- **Seven cases is a lead, not a finding.** The full study scales this to every HPD fire-damage
  vacate since 2018, with matched controls and a held-out test on later fires.
- **Some violations may follow the fire.** If a fire happened in late 2024 and the vacate order came in
  January 2025, post-fire inspections could count as "warnings." The full study only uses records
  from at least 60 days before each fire.
- **More complaints mean more inspections.** Buildings with active tenants generate more violations.
  The full study controls for complaint volume.

::: {.caveat}
Method: [how the comparison works](method.qmd). Code: `pilot/fire_analyze.py` and `pilot/pilot_stats.py`.
